RETRIEVAL DATES. config/layers.json has 6,365 cites, one per line. Only 608 have a true retrieval date: each has a record in docs/evidence/layers-mend-2026-10-20.json with "fetched": "2026-10-20", the URL and a quote or pointer. 607 match by passage, note, source, on and at. The 608th is genesis-50-20's Figures of Speech cite, which 0da9d1c re-pointed after the record was written.

For every other cite, the date it entered the repository was measured with a per-cite version of git log -S over all 25 commits that touched layers.json. Plain git blame is misleading here: 879e785 and 074cc0f re-sorted whole sections, so blame dates 1,025 older cites to round 2. Commits were then mapped to PRs through main's merges.

Proposed honest labels:
- retrieved 2026-10-20: 608 cites.
- retrieved 2026-10-20, moved: 2 cites (isaiah-7-9 and mark-12-10, in moved_outside_checked_notes).
- checked by 2026-10-11 (PR #38): 823 cites. Commits 1478aa0 to 1a8d291, 02:00 to 03:02 UTC. The PR says "all 1,143 were fetched again", but no URL or quote was kept.
- checked by 2026-10-11 (PR #39): 1 cite.
- checked by 2026-10-17 (PR #42): 1,533 cites. Quotes were matched against downloaded texts; only 33 Bible Hub quotes were re-fetched.
- checked by 2026-10-17 (PR #44): 3,373 cites. Matched against "sacred-texts files, the Companion Bible and Figures of Speech databases, Wesley".
- checked by 2026-10-17 (PR #45): 21 cites.
- cited 2026-10-17, not re-read since: 4 cites. These are the plain-meaning cites of the four returned passages. They entered in 47ec38b, were removed in 7c37488 and came back in 8e5a421 with no record, so they were never in a merged PR.

For the 4,927 round 2 cites, the words were checked against copies whose download date is not recorded, and usually not against the Bible Hub page the app links. No true retrieval date can be given for them.

Other problems found:
- 21 of the 608 were read on a different page than the one linked. 7 Companion Bible cites were read in archive.org's OCR of the printed book but link to StudyLight's index. 6 were read on StudyLight chapter pages but link to the index. 5 Figures of Speech cites were read in archive.org OCR text. 3 Themelios links differ only by www.
- 553 cites link to a whole work rather than a page: 431 Companion Bible cites go to the StudyLight index and 122 Figures of Speech cites go to the archive.org item.
- 610 cites have a page that was fetched on 2026-10-20 for a different cite. That page date is true, but their own point was not re-read, so they should keep their earlier label.

RE-FETCH. The cites link to 3,083 unique URLs: 2,992 on Bible Hub, of which 2,552 were not fetched on 2026-10-20. Adding exact pages for Bullinger (280 StudyLight chapters and 24 figure entries) makes 3,385 pages, about 28 minutes at 2 requests a second and about 0.3 to 0.6 GB. This is recommended as step 1: record URL, status, UTC time and SHA-256 for each page, check that the verse heading is there, and re-match the 608 stored quotes. Step 2 is reading the other 5,757 cites with a finder and a checker each, as the mend did. That is the real cost (several days of workflow, largest works first), and it is the only way to say "retrieved" truthfully for them and keep the evidence in the repository.

PUBLICATION DATES. These are given per work and per contributor for the books actually cited. Each is either checked on a dated title page or scan read on 2026-10-20 (archive.org identifiers given), or marked as not checked.

Corrections the cite list needs:
- gill: ends about 1766, not 1763 (dated OT volumes of 1764 and 1765).
- easton: 1893 was the first edition; 1897 was the third.
- henry-concise: CCEL calls it an abridgment by an unnamed editor, so it is not Henry's own wording from the early 1700s.
- Bible Hub's Barnes: Barnes wrote only the NT, Job, Psalms, Isaiah and Daniel. Genesis is J. G. Murphy (1866 scan), Hosea to Malachi is E. B. Pusey (1860 onward), and 141 cites on Numbers to Esther, Proverbs to Song, Jeremiah and Ezekiel have a writer not yet identified.
- Pulpit: Bible Hub shows only the Exposition. Expositors were read from title pages for 30 books, 4 more come from the voices list, and 14 books are unidentified. Per-volume first-edition years are not yet established; dated Kegan Paul printings run from 1881 to 1889.
- Ellicott, Keil and Delitzsch, JFB, Henry's continuators and Poole's continuators are given per book where sourced.
- Bible Hub's Strong's pages also display BDB and Thayer, both on the avoid list.

founderQuestions: Only 608 of the 6,365 Layers citations have a true retrieval date (2026-10-20). For the other 5,757, may the app show 'checked by 11 October 2026' or 'checked by 17 October 2026 against a copy of the text', or should it show no date until each page is re-read?

Shall we re-fetch all 3,385 cited pages now? That takes about 28 minutes at 2 requests a second and records the time, status and a hash for each page. Then, should every remaining cite be re-read and given a stored quote (several days of workflow, largest works first, starting with Gill, Barnes and JFB)?

For 21 cites the words were read on a different page than the one the reader is sent to, for example archive.org's scan of the printed Companion Bible rather than StudyLight's index. Should the credit link the page we actually read? And should all 553 Bullinger cites link the exact chapter or figure page instead of the whole work?

Bible Hub's 'Barnes' is not Barnes for most Old Testament books: Genesis is J. G. Murphy, the Minor Prophets are E. B. Pusey, and 141 cites are by a writer not yet identified. Do Murphy and Pusey (an Anglo-Catholic Tractarian) pass the citation rule? Until the others are identified, should those cites be hidden or kept with 'writer not yet confirmed'?

Henry's Concise Commentary (157 cites) is a later abridgment by an unnamed editor, not Henry's own wording. Should we keep it, credited as 'abridged from Matthew Henry', or move those cites to Henry's full commentary?

Several Ellicott and Pulpit contributors were flagged by the voices research: Aglen (Psalms, Song of Solomon, Jonah), Sanday, Plumptre, Farrar, Whitehouse and Plummer. Should those books get not_on entries, or should the cites stay with the true writer named?

The four returned plain-meaning cites (1 Samuel 6:6, Proverbs 3:20, Ecclesiastes 3:18 and 3:20) were never re-read in the mend. Should they be checked before the mend PR merges? And may the two moved cites (Isaiah 7:8 and Mark 12:1) carry 'retrieved 20 October 2026'?
